e.etymology: From the Catalan title of the Virgin Mary, Our Lady of Núria, named for a valley shrine in the Pyrenees. Some Muslim families use a separate name Nuria, from Arabic nur, light.
The English word beauty, from Old French beaute, from Latin bellus, pretty. As a given name it is used in the United States and widely in English-speaking Africa.

e.meaning: the Hebrew month of Sivan, in late spring
e.etymology: A month of the Hebrew calendar, falling in May and June, when Shavuot is celebrated. Its name came from Akkadian simanu, season. In Tamil, Sivan is a separate name of the god Shiva.
A feminine respelling of Cameron, a Scottish clan name from Gaelic cam sron, crooked nose.
Italy's most common surname, the plural of rosso, red, first a nickname for someone with red hair. As a given name it is close to Rosie.
From Hebrew Yotam, Yahweh is perfect or upright. In the Old Testament Jotham is the youngest son of Gideon, who tells the parable of the trees, and a king of Judah.
A form of Samira used in Bosnia, Ethiopia and Eritrea. Samira is Arabic for a companion in evening talk, the feminine of Samir.
A modern American name formed with the Ja- prefix, a variant of Jakari; compare Jabari and Kori.
Arabic Umayr, the diminutive of Umar, from a root meaning to live long and thrive. Several companions of the Prophet Muhammad bore the name; it is especially common in Pakistan.
A spelling of Ziyad, common in Egypt, from Arabic ziyada, increase or abundance. Tariq ibn Ziyad led the Muslim crossing into Spain in 711.
A modern American name combining the Ja- prefix with Leigha, a spelling of Leah; it sounds the same as Jaliyah.
A spelling of Adalyn or Adeline, from the French pet form of Adele, built on the Germanic element adal, noble.
Arabic basma, a smile, from the verb basama, to smile. Related names include Basim and Bassam for boys.
From Sanskrit parama, highest or supreme. Among Sikhs it is also a short form of names such as Paramjit and Parampreet.
Arabic Zaydan, an extended form of Zayd, from the root zada, to grow or increase. The surname of French soccer star Zinedine Zidane is the same name.
A K spelling of Callum, the Scottish Gaelic form of Latin Columba, dove. Saint Columba founded the monastery of Iona in the sixth century.
A modern American name in the family of Nyja, Naja and Nia.
e.note: Naija is the everyday nickname Nigerians use for Nigeria and things Nigerian.

e.etymology: A variant of Holton, an English place name and surname ending in Old English tun, farm or settlement. Holten is also a Danish surname and a town in the Netherlands.
A Latin American pet form of Yuliana and Julia, and in Hebrew the word for July, used for girls and boys. All go back to the Roman family name Julius.
A modern American name that blends the sounds of Kyler, Tyler and Kayden.
A transliteration of Hebrew Betsal'el, in the shadow of God, meaning under his protection. In Exodus, Bezalel is the master craftsman who builds the Tabernacle and the Ark of the Covenant.
A Z spelling of Sarai, Sarah's name in Genesis before God renames her, traditionally read as my princess. The form Zaraí is used in Latin America.
A double-l spelling of Emilia, the feminine of the Roman family name Aemilius, usually linked to Latin aemulus, rival or striving.
A spelling of Henrik or Hendrick, the Scandinavian and Dutch forms of Henry, from Germanic heim, home, and ric, ruler.
A respelling of Sinai, the mountain where Moses receives the Ten Commandments in Exodus. The origin of the place name is uncertain.
A modern Israeli name from Hebrew noy, beauty or ornament; some read the ending as a short form of God's name, giving beauty of God. It is unrelated to Noa.
A respelling of Camila or Kamila. Camila is from the Roman family name Camillus, linked to a word for a youth who assisted at religious rites; the Arabic name Kamila means perfect or complete.
Arabic haydar, lion, a title of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law, honored for his courage. The name is especially loved among Shia Muslims.
A modern name that extends Kai with the -yan ending of Kiyan, Ayan and Rayan.
The Portuguese word and name for sapphire, a form of Sapphira, from Greek sappheiros, a blue gemstone. It is also used in Indonesia; in Arabic, safira separately means a woman ambassador.
A spelling of Leonie, from French Léonie, the feminine of Leon, from Latin leo, lion. Leoni is also an Italian surname.
In Turkish, Nil is the Nile River and a girls' name. As a boys' name it is a spelling of the Indian name Neel, from Sanskrit nila, dark blue, and in Catalan a form of the saint's name Nilus.
e.note: In English nil means nothing or zero, as in a sports score.

assoc.t: nil, the word for nothing or zero
